title: Matters before the Rajasthan High Court: Writs, Appeals and Revisions
excerpt: Civil writ petitions (CWP), including miscellaneous service matters and matters against development authorities, and civil and criminal appeals and revisions follow a defined procedure at Jaipur.
body: I appear before the Rajasthan High Court in civil writ petitions, including miscellaneous service matters and matters against development authorities, in civil and criminal appeals and revisions, and in other petitions.

A writ petition under Article 226 requires a legal right, a corresponding duty, and a breach. Delay, suppression of material facts, and an adequate alternative remedy are frequent grounds of dismissal at the threshold. Certified copies and a precise prayer are essential.
Appeals and revisions from civil and criminal orders are presented in accordance with the High Court Rules. Limitation, the paper-book, and the stay application are considered at the first listing.
This note is for general information. Whether a writ, appeal or revision lies in a given case depends on the order under challenge and the record.

title: RERA Rajasthan: Complaints, Appeals and Execution
excerpt: Complaints before RERA, the Adjudicating Officer and the Real Estate Appellate Tribunal, together with JDA Appellate Tribunal work and property suits.
body: I handle complaints, appeals and execution proceedings before RERA Rajasthan, the Adjudicating Officer and the Real Estate Appellate Tribunal. I also appear in development authority disputes before the JDA Appellate Tribunal, and in property disputes before civil courts.

A complaint under the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act may seek refund, interest, possession, or compensation. The promoter, the project registration, and the builder–buyer agreement are the core of the papers.
Orders of the Authority or the Adjudicating Officer are appealed to the Real Estate Appellate Tribunal within the statutory period. Execution follows if the order is not complied with.
This note outlines the ordinary route. The correct forum depends on the relief sought and the stage of the project.

title: Consumer Commissions: Deficiency in Service, Builder–Buyer and Insurance
excerpt: Complaints, appeals and execution before District and State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions.
body: I represent consumers and service providers before District and State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions. This includes complaints, appeals and execution proceedings in matters of deficiency in service, builder–buyer disputes, and insurance, banking and product-related claims.
Jurisdiction depends on the value of goods or services and the compensation claimed. Limitation is two years from the date of the cause of action, subject to condonation for sufficient cause.

The complaint should annex invoices, correspondence, and a precise statement of the deficiency and the relief sought. Commercial purpose, except for self-employment, ordinarily takes the transaction outside the Act.
This note is general. Whether a complaint is maintainable turns on the contract and the facts.

title: Section 138 NI Act: Notice, Complaint, Trial, Appeal and Revision
excerpt: Cheque dishonour claims are lost on procedure more often than on merits. The statutory sequence must be followed.
body: I act for complainants and accused persons in cheque dishonour cases under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. My work covers the statutory legal notice, the complaint, trial, appeal and revision.

The cheque must be presented within its period of validity. Upon dishonour, a written demand must be made within thirty days of receiving information from the bank. The drawer then has fifteen days to make payment. A complaint may be filed within one month of the expiry of that period.

The complainant must prove the debt or liability, the issue of the cheque, presentation, dishonour, and service of the demand notice. Defences commonly taken include absence of a legally enforceable debt and failure of the statutory notice. Compounding remains available.
This note does not replace advice on a particular cheque or notice.

title: Family Courts: Divorce, Maintenance, Custody and Domestic Violence
excerpt: Divorce, maintenance, custody and guardianship, together with domestic violence proceedings before family courts and magistrate courts.
body: I handle divorce, maintenance, custody and guardianship matters, along with domestic violence proceedings and related criminal matters, before family courts and magistrate courts.

Divorce by mutual consent requires a joint petition, a waiting period, and the court’s satisfaction as to free consent. Contested petitions proceed on cruelty, desertion or the other statutory grounds. Settlement of maintenance, residence and custody should be reduced to writing.
Applications under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act may seek protection, residence, monetary relief and custody. Interim orders are available on a prima facie case.
This note is a general outline. Seek advice before signing any terms or filing any petition.

title: Civil Suits: Recovery, Injunction, Specific Performance and Order 37
excerpt: Suits for recovery of money, declaration, injunction, specific performance etc., including summary suits under Order 37 CPC.
body: I appear in civil suits for recovery of money, declaration, injunction, specific performance etc. This includes summary suits under Order 37 CPC, appeals and execution proceedings.

A temporary injunction requires a prima facie case, balance of convenience and irreparable injury. Specific performance requires a concluded contract and continuous readiness and willingness to perform.

Summary suits under Order 37 are available on bills of exchange, hundies, promissory notes, and written contracts for a liquidated demand. Leave to defend is granted where a substantial defence is disclosed.
This note outlines the ordinary remedies. The correct suit depends on the writing and the relief sought.

title: Commercial Courts: Contracts, Supply Agreements and Partnerships
excerpt: Disputes before Commercial Courts arising from contracts, supply and service agreements, partnerships and business transactions.
body: I represent businesses in disputes before Commercial Courts arising from contracts, supply and service agreements, partnerships and business transactions.

The Commercial Courts Act requires that a suit of specified value, arising from a commercial dispute, be filed before the Commercial Court. Pre-institution mediation is required in suits that do not contemplate urgent interim relief.
The plaintiff must file a statement of truth and the documents relied upon. Case-management, verification of documents, and costs for delay are stricter than in an ordinary civil suit.
This note outlines the forum. Whether a claim is a commercial dispute of specified value depends on the contract and the amount.

title: Arbitration and ADR: Section 9, Appointment of Arbitrators and Awards
excerpt: Arbitral proceedings and court applications under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, including mediation and conciliation.
body: I appear in arbitral proceedings and in court applications under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, including Section 9 interim relief, appointment of arbitrators, and challenges to and enforcement of awards. I also advise on mediation and conciliation.

Section 9 permits interim measures before or during the arbitration, and after the award but before it is enforced. An application for appointment of an arbitrator lies where the agreement names no arbitrator or the named person fails to act.
A challenge to an award under Section 34 is not an appeal. The grounds are those listed in the Act. Limitation is short and is counted from receipt of the award.
This note is informational and does not advise on any particular clause or award.

title: SARFAESI and DRT: Applications for Borrowers and Guarantors
excerpt: Securitisation applications under the SARFAESI Act and proceedings before the Debts Recovery Tribunal.
body: I file securitisation applications under the SARFAESI Act and appear in proceedings before the Debts Recovery Tribunal. I act for borrowers and guarantors in recovery proceedings.

After classification of the account as a non-performing asset, a secured creditor may issue a demand notice and, on default, take possession of the secured asset. Sale is by public auction after valuation and publication.
An aggrieved borrower or any person may apply to the Debts Recovery Tribunal under Section 17. Limitation is short. Deposit as a condition of stay of sale is common.
This note is a general account of the sequence and is not advice on any particular loan or notice.

title: Corporate Advisory: Companies, LLPs, Startups and Due Diligence
excerpt: Day-to-day legal requirements, commercial transactions, and legal due diligence for land and business transactions.
body: I advise companies, LLPs, partnership firms and startups on their day-to-day legal requirements and commercial transactions. I also conduct legal due diligence for land and business transactions.
Advisory work includes reviewing proposed contracts, identifying regulatory requirements, and setting out the risks of a transaction in writing before papers are signed.
Legal due diligence for land and business transactions covers title, encumbrances, licences, pending litigation, and the authority of the persons signing.
This note is general. Advice on a particular company or transaction is given only after the papers are reviewed.

title: Contract Drafting: Development, Sale, Lease, Franchise and Partnership
excerpt: Drafting and review of the agreements that real estate, commercial and partnership transactions require.
body: I draft and review contracts, including development agreements and joint venture agreements; agreements to sell and builder–buyer agreements; lease and leave-and-licence agreements; franchise, service, supply and vendor agreements; partnership deeds and LLP agreements; and memoranda of understanding and settlement agreements.

A well-drawn agreement identifies the parties, the consideration, the timeline, the events of default, and the forum for disputes. Stamp duty and registration requirements must be considered before execution.

Builder–buyer and development agreements should be consistent with RERA where the project is registered. Settlement agreements should be capable of being placed before a court or tribunal if enforcement is later required.
This note is informational. The terms of any agreement depend on the transaction and the parties.

title: Non-Litigation Work: Title Search, Deeds, Notices and Registration
excerpt: Title verification, due diligence, deeds, legal notices, representations before authorities, and assistance with document registration.
body: My non-litigation work includes title search, title verification and legal opinions on property; legal due diligence for land, warehouse, hotel and commercial projects; drafting of sale deeds, gift deeds, relinquishment deeds, wills and powers of attorney; legal notices and replies; representations before government departments and development authorities; and assistance with document registration.

A title opinion is based on the chain of documents, the revenue record, and searches for encumbrances and pending litigation. It is not a guarantee of title; it is a reasoned view of the papers produced.

Deeds must be stamped and, where the law requires, registered. A power of attorney used for transfer of immovable property has its own formalities. Legal notices should state the facts, the demand, and a reasonable time for compliance.
This note describes the ordinary non-litigation work of the practice. Advice on a particular property or deed follows a review of the documents.
